description: Add tests for the new fixes - rate limiting, memory leak eviction, timeout handling, cron health, and response envelope
steps: 1. Create tests/unit/rate-limit-mutating-coverage.test.ts that verifies the rate limit utility works correctly for the entities added (bulk operations entity keys). Test that rateLimitMutating returns null when under limit and returns a 429 Response when over limit.

2. Create tests/unit/memory-leak-fixes.test.ts that verifies: (a) critical-error-alert rateLimitMap respects max size, (b) deprecation registry respects max entries, (c) log-stream clients Map respects max clients and cleans up dead connections, (d) email router resets daily counts

3. Create tests/unit/cron-health.test.ts that verifies: (a) registerCronRun() stores the timestamp, (b) getCronHealth() returns all registered crons with their last-run times, (c) the Map is bounded (doesn't grow beyond MAX_CRONS), (d) stale detection works (crons not run in > expected interval are flagged)

4. Create tests/unit/response-envelope.test.ts that verifies: (a) envelope() wraps data correctly, (b) paginatedEnvelope() includes meta with page/limit/total, (c) errorEnvelope() produces the correct error shape
acceptance_criteria: All new test files pass with npx vitest run
Tests verify the bounded/eviction behavior of the memory leak fixes
Tests cover the cron health monitoring utility
Tests cover the response envelope helper
verification: npx vitest run tests/unit/rate-limit-mutating-coverage.test.ts tests/unit/memory-leak-fixes.test.ts tests/unit/cron-health.test.ts tests/unit/response-envelope.test.ts
findings: All 38 tests pass. Node.js needed to be installed via mise (node@20). The critical-error-alert test required advancing fake timers past the 1s internal await. Pre-existing TS errors exist in unrelated files but do not affect our test files. mise.toml was created as a side-effect of installing node.
